sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A cultivated bulbous herb about 60 cm tall. Its rounded bulb contains up to about 15 cloves beneath a papery coat. The leaves are long and flat; greenish-white or pinkish flowers form an umbel that may also contain bulbils. Kew gives Central Asia and northeastern Iran as its native range; garlic is now widely cultivated.

sections.title: Food and comparison
sections.text: Kew records food use of all parts, although the bulb is the part most commonly eaten. Unlike Welsh onion (Allium fistulosum), garlic forms a distinct bulb divided into cloves.
